feed.title: A Box of Tools
feed.subtitle: Free browser tools that never upload your files. Combine images into a PDF or an MP4, compress an image to an exact size, crop a video, or strip EXIF data.

entry.title: How to share text and files between devices without uploading them
entry.summary: Move text or files from one browser to another over a direct encrypted connection - no email-to-self, no chat history, no account, and nothing stored on any server to delete later.

entry.title: Base64 Encoder & Decoder
entry.summary: Encode and decode Base64 in both alphabets, percent-encode URLs, escape HTML entities, and read hex and backslash escapes. It all runs in your browser - nothing is uploaded, so a token never leaves your machine.

entry.title: How to check a download against its checksum
entry.summary: How to check an MD5 or SHA-256 checksum on Windows, macOS and Linux or in your browser, what a match actually proves, and the mistake that makes the whole exercise pointless.

entry.title: How to clean up a voice memo before sending it
entry.summary: Cut the dead air and the false starts, then bring the level up to full scale. Two browser tools in a row, in the order that keeps the quality, and the recording never leaves your machine.

entry.title: How to combine images into one PDF
entry.summary: Turn photos or scans into a single PDF: page size, order and rotation, why a JPEG need not lose any quality on the way in, and what a PDF tells the person you send it to.

entry.title: How to compare two JSON files
entry.summary: Format both files the same way, sort the keys, then diff them. Why a raw JSON diff is mostly noise, how to canonicalise both sides in the browser, and what survives to the patch.

entry.title: How to compress an image to an exact file size
entry.summary: An upload form wants 500 KB and your photo is 4 MB. What a size limit really costs, which setting to move first, and why a PNG will not shrink the way a JPEG does.

entry.title: How to convert an SVG to a PNG at the right size
entry.summary: A vector has no pixel size of its own, so the number is yours to choose. Where that number comes from for a screen, an app icon and a printer, and what changes when a drawing becomes pixels.

entry.title: How to crop a video to a different shape
entry.summary: Cut a clip down to a square, a 9:16 portrait, or an exact pixel box. Which ratio each platform wants, why cropping has to re-encode when trimming does not, and what that costs.

entry.title: How to edit a GIF frame by frame
entry.summary: Take a GIF apart into its frames, drop or reorder them, and rebuild it with the timing kept. What survives the round trip, what the palette costs, and how to see why a GIF is heavy.

entry.title: How to format JSON without handing it to anybody
entry.summary: How to lay out, check and minify JSON in your own browser - what a formatter must never change about your file, how to read the error message, and why the site you paste it into matters.

entry.title: How to get phone photos ready for the web
entry.summary: HEIC to JPEG, GPS stripped, resized for the page and compressed to a budget - the whole pipeline in the browser, and the originals never leave your machine.

entry.title: How to make a GIF from part of a video
entry.summary: Cut the seconds that matter first, then convert only those. When the GIF converter's own timeline is enough, when to cut with the video cutter instead, and why every second of GIF costs so much.

entry.title: How to make a PDF smaller, and why some will not shrink
entry.summary: Where a PDF's size actually is, why a scan compresses 80% and a contract barely moves, what DPI means here, and what a compressor should never do to your document.

entry.title: How to make a QR code and prove it scans
entry.summary: Generate the code, then verify it with a reader on the same site - the exact payload, the real link, at print size and from a photo - before the print run. All in the browser, nothing uploaded.

entry.title: How to make a QR code that still scans on somebody else's phone
entry.summary: Which error-correction level to pick, why the white margin around a QR code is part of the code, how big to print it, and what a free generator's 'dynamic' code costs you later.

entry.title: How to make a boomerang video
entry.summary: Cut the moment, reverse the copy, join the two, and loop it. Three tools in a row, all running in your browser, and the order that keeps the whole job down to a minute.

entry.title: How to make a favicon that still reads at sixteen pixels
entry.summary: Which sizes a favicon.ico actually needs, which extra files iPhones, Android and a Mac ask for, and why a logo that works on a poster disappears at sixteen pixels.

entry.title: How to make a video thumbnail from the exact right frame
entry.summary: Step to the precise frame, save it losslessly, size it for the platform, and hit the byte limit. Three browser tools in a row, and the footage never leaves your machine.

entry.title: How to make an animated GIF from images
entry.summary: Turn a set of pictures into one animated GIF: how fast a GIF can really play, what the palette setting changes, and the three things that actually make the file smaller.

entry.title: How to merge, split and reorder PDF pages
entry.summary: Combine PDFs, cut one into several, and move pages around: what survives the reshuffle, what no tool can carry across, and why none of it needs uploading your documents anywhere.

entry.title: How to open a DICOM file, and what is in one
entry.summary: What is on a hospital disc, why the files have no extension, how to open a .dcm scan in a browser, what window and level actually does, and what a scan carries about the patient besides the picture.

entry.title: How to redact a PDF so the text is really gone
entry.summary: A black box drawn in a PDF reader usually leaves the words underneath it, and copy-and-paste gets them straight back. What a real redaction removes, the four places a word hides outside the page, and how to check a file before you send it.

entry.title: How to redact an image so the hidden part is really gone
entry.summary: Black boxes drawn in most programs sit on top of the picture and can be moved aside. What separates a real redaction from a covered one, why pixelated text can be read back, and how to check a file before you send it.

entry.title: How to resize an image without wrecking it
entry.summary: What happens to a picture when you change its pixel dimensions: why shrinking is safe and enlarging is not, what to do when the box is the wrong shape, and when to crop instead.

entry.title: How to reverse a video
entry.summary: Play a clip backwards: what reversing does to the picture and the sound, why it cannot be done without re-encoding, why it is slower than trimming, and what to do first.

entry.title: How to save a frame from a video as a picture
entry.summary: Get a still out of a clip at its real resolution: why a screenshot of a paused player is not the same picture, which format to save it in, and how to land on the exact frame you meant.

entry.title: How to scan a document with your phone
entry.summary: What separates a photograph of a page from a scan of one: the angle, the uneven light, and the file size. How to take the photo, what to fix afterwards, and why none of it needs a server.

entry.title: How to scan multiple pages into one small PDF
entry.summary: Photograph every page, get one PDF, combine it with documents you already have, and shrink it until it sends. Three browser tools in a row, and the paperwork never leaves your phone.

entry.title: How to split a GIF into frames
entry.summary: Get every frame of an animated GIF as a PNG: why some frames are only a small patch of the picture, what happens to the transparency, and how to keep the timing so you can put it back together.
